training-load.short: How much training stress a session or a week puts on you, combining how long and how hard. It can be counted from what you did or from how your body responded.

external-load.short: The work you did, measured outside the body: time, distance, pace, watts, kilojoules. The same for anyone who did the same session.

internal-load.short: How hard a session was for your body: heart rate, perceived effort, lactate. The same external load can give a different internal load on a hot day or when tired.

session-rpe.short: One effort rating (0–10) for a whole session, given about 30 minutes after it, multiplied by its duration in minutes to give a load score.

arbitrary-unit.short: A score with no physical meaning of its own, such as 'RPE × minutes'. Useful to compare one athlete's sessions; not convertible into joules or watts.

trimp.short: A load score from heart rate: minutes of training weighted by how high the heart rate was. Banister, Edwards and Lucia each proposed a version.

normalised-power.short: A power figure that weights the hard parts of a ride more than plain average power: 30-s rolling averages, each raised to the 4th power, averaged, then the 4th root taken.

intensity-factor.short: Normalised power divided by FTP. IF 1.0 means the ride was, in this sense, as hard as threshold; 0.7 is an easy endurance ride.

tss.short: A load score from power: hours × IF² × 100, so one hour at FTP gives 100. A commercial metric; running and swimming versions use pace instead of power.

fitness-fatigue-model.short: A model in which each session adds both 'fitness' (slow to fade) and 'fatigue' (quick to fade); predicted performance is fitness minus fatigue.

ctl.short: A slowly changing average of daily training load, by default with a 42-day time constant. Often labelled 'fitness' in training apps.

atl.short: A quickly changing average of daily training load, by default with a 7-day time constant. Often labelled 'fatigue' in training apps.

tsb.short: CTL minus ATL, often called 'form'. Negative after hard weeks, rising towards positive in a taper.

overfitting.short: When a model has so many adjustable numbers that it fits past data well but predicts new data badly: it has learned the noise.

acwr.short: Last week's training load divided by the average weekly load of the last four weeks. Proposed as an injury-risk marker; now heavily criticised.

ewma.short: An average in which each older day counts a bit less than the one after it, instead of all days counting equally.

mathematical-coupling.short: When the same number appears on both sides of a comparison (here, last week's load inside both parts of a ratio), creating a correlation that has nothing to do with biology.

wellness-questionnaire.short: A short daily self-rating of sleep, fatigue, soreness, stress and mood, often each on a 1–5 scale, used to track how an athlete is coping with training.

overreaching.short: A drop in performance after a block of heavy training. 'Functional' if it recovers in days to a couple of weeks, 'non-functional' if it lasts weeks.

ln-rmssd.short: The natural log of RMSSD, the usual HRV number for daily monitoring. The log evens out its spread so averages behave better. A change of 0.1 in ln rMSSD is roughly a 10% change in RMSSD.
